Suzuki Jimny Sierra II with a rooftop tent, 2 guests, Oct 10–12. Booked under Asuka Umeda.
          Pick up 11:00, drop off 18:00 — but airport return closes 17:30.

Warm and still swimmable; nights near 24 °C. Showers pass quickly, but wind is the real threat on an exposed pitch. October is still typhoon season — roughly a 1-in-10 chance of one within 300 km over three days, so keep a wet-weather fallback.
Free, right on the sand, closest site to the airport. Toilets. Busy at weekends.
Managed park with direct beach access, car camping, kayak and SUP rental.
Wide mown lawn, sunrise over Kudaka Island, clean toilets and six pavilions.
Free sunrise-side beach, good stargazing, Cape Chinen a short drive on.
Calm bay with sunsets over the city. No toilets.
Forest site with spacious plots and designated cooking areas — fire rules are clear here.
Quiet bay, calm water, no toilets.
Sheltered riverside pull-in with water and clean toilets.
Managed site near Nago with showers, toilets and Wi-Fi. Lower pitches shelter well in bad weather.
Auto camping and bungalows with BBQ facilities; boat and kayak rental.
Views of Kouri Bridge and ocean sunsets. Room for one car.
Secluded strip of coast that feels private, with ocean sunsets.
Beachside, mountain and VIP pitches over emerald water. Bookable.
Shaded sunset-side pitch looking across to Kouri Bridge. Park well back from the tide line.
Sunset beach with a michi-no-eki and konbini next door.
Simple and quiet, with toilets, showers, grills and fire pits — the easiest BBQ of the north.
Grassy riverside clearing under tall trees. Nothing but the river.
Beachside, riverside and VIP pitches with access to water sports.
Free sunset beach with free toilets and showers. Shared with day visitors at weekends.
Straightforward beach pitch with clear-night skies and good sunsets.
Some of the best stargazing up north, with toilets, showers and a kitchen.
Where the Benoki River meets the sea — almost no light pollution.
Pitches under forest canopy deep in Yanbaru, with toilets and showers.
Local spot with ocean views, sunrises and dark skies. No toilet or shower.
Shaded pitch on the north-east coast about 3 km below Cape Hedo, fringed by reef.
Secluded turquoise bay 10 min from Cape Hedo, with parking and showers.
Fried-to-order sata andagi, ¥150. Sweets Hyakumeiten 2026, and the Churaumi discount tickets are sold here.
Fifty-year-old shokudo whose milk zenzai is a Nago institution.
One item since 1948, beans cooked over a wood fire. Ten minutes from Churaumi.
The mango ice mountain that defines Okinawan shaved ice. Hyakumeiten 2026.
At the Zakimi Castle gate; fine ice with Yomitan purple sweet potato.
The one serious modern kakigori shop in the centre. Twelve seats and it sells out.
Upstairs at the Cape Hedo visitor centre — East China Sea to Pacific in one view.
Hilltop red-tiled house looking out to Ie-jima. The most photographed view cafe on the island.
Terrace on the sand inside the Bise fukugi grove, facing Ie-jima. Opens at 08:00.
Hammock seats on a hillside, and bukubuku-cha you will not find elsewhere.
Hoshino Resorts cliff cafe built into the rocks; 160 outdoor seats, shuts an hour after sunset.
Rooftop over American Village with the sea at eye level.
150 seats, 07:00–22:00 — the reliable fallback when the seawall branch is mobbed.
The original beni-imo tart, at the flagship with a factory window.
The 1963 flagship with a retro diner interior. Beni-imo and salt-chinsuko scoops.
Fruit tarts in the old American housing district — a photogenic detour in itself.
Naturally leavened bread and scones. The best edible souvenir for a camping trip — no fridge needed.

Every drivable campsite in the Evertrail directory — 26 sites on the main island,
      ordered by road time from Naha Airport within each region. Ferry-only islands are left out. The directory
      lists a fee for only two of them, so treat “none posted” as unknown rather than free, and book the
      paid sites — Oct 10–12 is the Sports Day long weekend.

Shaved ice, cafes and sweets, all checked open on our three dates. The day number is where each
      one fits the drive. It is a long weekend, so the famous ones will have a queue.
One backpack each. Bedding and the BBQ set come with the rental, so this is what we carry plus what we buy on landing. Tap a row to check it off, or Edit list to change it.

Night 1 is covered, night 2 is not. The set is one dinner for two — 200 g agu pork, 200 g Okinawa beef, two sausages, four yakitori, gas and the teppan grill. Buy tomorrow's meat on day 2, not today; a cooler will not hold it through two days at 28 °C.

Habu season. The prefecture runs its snake-bite campaign 1 Sep–30 Nov — October is peak activity, and Yanbaru is core habitat. Torch after dark, closed shoes off-trail, never reach into long grass or stone walls, and shake out your boots in the morning.

Return the car by 17:30, not 18:00. The booking's 18:00 slot is the Evertrail office; airport return closes at 17:30. Today is also Sports Day, a national holiday — expect traffic on Route 58 and a busy terminal.
The published coordinate lands on the expressway, so the drive time is unreliable. Scout it first.
Under a road bridge in urban Nago — no beach, no view. Not recommended.
One car only — risky on a holiday weekend with a rooftop tent.
Dead-end track, very little room, and you reverse back out.
No facilities, off-road access, riverside in typhoon season. Not recommended.
Routing uses narrow forest roads that close after storms. Allow longer via Route 70.
